# Otjiherero Dictionary

> A community dictionary for Otjiherero (Herero, Bantu language of Namibia and
> Angola) with bilingual lookup and dictionary-grounded sentence translation.

The site is a PWA. Its structured dictionary data is available for reuse:

- Machine-readable lexicon: `/lexicon.json` — all English headwords with
  Otjiherero terms, noun-class (singular/plural) prefixes, and example
  sentence pairs. The shape is documented below.
- Sitemap: `/sitemap.xml`
- Human pages: `/` (search + browse), `/translate` (bidirectional lookup and
  RAG sentence translation)

## Lexicon JSON shape

```json
{
  "entries": [{
    "id": "w001",
    "en": "WOMAN",              // headword as printed
    "lemma": "WOMAN",           // headword without homograph suffix
    "terms": [{ "hz": "omukazendu", "classPrefix": "ova" }],
    "subEntries": [{ "en": "OLD", "hz": "omukurukaze" }],
    "examples": [{ "en": "THE CHILD IS WET", "hz": "Omuatje wa ningena" }]
  }],
  "hzIndex": [{ "hz": "omukazendu", "en": "WOMAN", "entryId": "w001" }]
}
```

`classPrefix` is the plural noun-class prefix (`ova-`, `ovi-`, `ozo-`, …);
Otjiherero nouns agree with their class on verbs and adjectives.

## MCP server

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server ships with the repo so AI assistants
can query the dictionary as tools:

- `lookup_word` — bidirectional word lookup (offline)
- `search_dictionary` — retrieve the entries the translator is grounded in
- `translate_sentence` — full RAG translation (needs `LLM_API_KEY`)
- `get_lexicon_stats` — corpus size and data-quality flags
- resource `dictionary://lexicon` — the full lexicon JSON

Setup: build with `npm run mcp:build`, then register
`node dist-mcp/mcp-server.mjs` in your MCP client (see `.mcp.json`).
